# Model Fitting Setup Validation

Make the estimand and fitted data explicit before comparing or accepting
models.

## Setup

Resolve the applicable choices:

- requested output: prediction, optimum location, response at the optimum,
  model metric, coefficient, p-value, class, or another quantity;
- response and predictor definitions, units, transformations, and category or
  event orientation;
- included row scope, controls, baselines, endpoints, missing values, and
  replicate handling;
- candidate models, formulas, fixed parameters, and fitting implementation;
- comparison metric and convention; and
- evaluation or optimization domain and final extraction rule.

These choices must follow the task and data semantics rather than tool defaults
or whichever rows are easiest to fit.

## Row And Predictor Scope

- Fit compared candidates on the same effective observations unless the task
  explicitly defines different subsets. Verify row counts after filtering,
  formula evaluation, and missing-value handling.
- Include a control or boundary row only when it belongs to the modeled
  response curve or estimand. Exclude unrelated controls, backgrounds, or
  component systems.
- Preserve raw replicates, paired observations, or aggregated entities according
  to the experimental unit. Do not silently average repeated labels.
- For ratios, mixtures, doses, frequencies, or proportions, identify the focal
  component and token order from component labels or documented metadata before
  converting text to a numeric predictor. Equal ratio strings do not imply the
  same predictor when their component systems differ.
- For a two-component proportion axis, pure rows measured under the same assay,
  response definition, background, and component system are candidate observed
  boundaries: the pure focal component is `p=1` and the pure counterpart is
  `p=0`. Treat the endpoints symmetrically. Include both when the estimand is the
  full response curve; exclude both when the task explicitly restricts the fit
  to interior mixtures. Do not include only the endpoint that produces a
  preferred fit.
- If endpoint membership is genuinely ambiguous and materially affects the
  requested result, compare the interior-only scope with the complete set of
  same-system observed boundaries while holding every other modeling choice
  fixed. Select a scope from task and data semantics, not from the resulting
  answer.

## Model Comparison

- Compare metrics only across compatible response definitions, likelihoods,
  transformations, and effective row sets.
- Confirm each formula, basis, parameter count, observation count, and metric
  convention that affects the comparison.
- For likelihood-derived criteria such as AIC, do not compare values from
  incompatible likelihoods or differently scoped data.
- Keep event/reference classes explicit for binary or categorical models before
  interpreting probabilities or coefficient signs.

## Evaluation And Optimization

- Use the domain specified by the task. Otherwise use the valid observed range
  after the accepted row-scope decision; do not extrapolate silently.
- Distinguish an optimum's location from the fitted response at that location.
- Extract the requested value from the accepted fitted result, not from a
  different empirical summary or a refitted replacement.

Before finalizing, verify that the actual fitted rows, model, metric, domain,
and extracted quantity match these decisions.

input.content:
# Read data
dat <- read.csv("inputs/Swarm_2.csv", sep = ",", header = TRUE)
cat("Raw data rows:", nrow(dat), "\n")

# Inspect StrainNumber and Ratio values
cat("\nUnique StrainNumber values:\n")
print(unique(dat$StrainNumber))
cat("\nRatio by StrainNumber:\n")
print(table(dat$StrainNumber, dat$Ratio))

# Build proportion of strain 287
# For mixtures 287_98, Ratio is "X:Y" meaning 287:98
# proportion of 287 = X/(X+Y)
# For pure 287 (StrainNumber=287, Ratio=1:0) -> proportion = 1
# For pure 98 (StrainNumber=98, Ratio=1:0) -> proportion = 0
# For pure 1 -> exclude

dat$prop287 <- NA

for (i in 1:nrow(dat)) {
  sn <- as.character(dat$StrainNumber[i])
  rat <- as.character(dat$Ratio[i])

  if (sn == "287" && rat == "1:0") {
    dat$prop287[i] <- 1.0
  } else if (sn == "98" && rat == "1:0") {
    dat$prop287[i] <- 0.0
  } else if (sn == "287_98") {
    parts <- as.numeric(strsplit(rat, ":")[[1]])
    dat$prop287[i] <- parts[1] / (parts[1] + parts[2])
  }
  # else stays NA (strain 1, excluded)
}

# Subset to relevant rows
fitdat <- subset(dat, !is.na(prop287))
cat("\nRows for modeling:", nrow(fitdat), "\n")
cat("\nData summary:\n")
print(fitdat[, c("StrainNumber", "Ratio", "prop287", "Area")])

cat("\nProportion values:\n")
print(sort(unique(fitdat$prop287)))

# Fit models
# Quadratic: Area ~ prop287 + I(prop287^2)
m_quad <- lm(Area ~ prop287 + I(prop287^2), data = fitdat)
cat("\n=== Quadratic Model ===\n")
cat("AIC:", AIC(m_quad), "\n")
cat("Coefficients:\n")
print(summary(m_quad)$coefficients)
cat("R-squared:", summary(m_quad)$r.squared, "\n")

# Cubic: Area ~ prop287 + I(prop287^2) + I(prop287^3)
m_cubic <- lm(Area ~ prop287 + I(prop287^2) + I(prop287^3), data = fitdat)
cat("\n=== Cubic Model ===\n")
cat("AIC:", AIC(m_cubic), "\n")
cat("Coefficients:\n")
print(summary(m_cubic)$coefficients)
cat("R-squared:", summary(m_cubic)$r.squared, "\n")

# Natural spline df=4
library(splines)
m_ns <- lm(Area ~ ns(prop287, df = 4), data = fitdat)
cat("\n=== Natural Spline (df=4) Model ===\n")
cat("AIC:", AIC(m_ns), "\n")
cat("R-squared:", summary(m_ns)$r.squared, "\n")
cat("Effective df:", length(coef(m_ns)), "parameters\n")

# Compare AICs
aics <- c(Quadratic = AIC(m_quad), Cubic = AIC(m_cubic), NaturalSpline = AIC(m_ns))
cat("\n=== AIC Comparison ===\n")
print(aics)
cat("Best model (lowest AIC):", names(which.min(aics)), "\n")

# Select best model
best_name <- names(which.min(aics))
best_model <- switch(best_name,
  Quadratic = m_quad,
  Cubic = m_cubic,
  NaturalSpline = m_ns
)

# Find optimal proportion (maximizing predicted Area) within [0, 1]
# Use optimization
obj_fn <- function(p) {
  newdat <- data.frame(prop287 = p)
  -predict(best_model, newdata = newdat)
}

# Try optimize
opt <- optimize(obj_fn, interval = c(0, 1), maximum = FALSE)
cat("\n=== Optimal Proportion ===\n")
cat("Optimal p:", opt$minimum, "\n")

# Predicted Area at optimum
pred_opt <- predict(best_model, newdata = data.frame(prop287 = opt$minimum))
cat("Maximum predicted Area:", pred_opt, "\n")

# Also do a fine grid search as verification
pgrid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 10001)
preds <- predict(best_model, newdata = data.frame(prop287 = pgrid))
grid_max_idx <- which.max(preds)
cat("\nGrid search verification:\n")
cat("Optimal p (grid):", pgrid[grid_max_idx], "\n")
cat("Max Area (grid):", preds[grid_max_idx], "\n")

# Plot for sanity check
pdf("model_fit.pdf", width = 10, height = 6)
plot(fitdat$prop287, fitdat$Area,
     xlab = "Proportion of strain 287",
     ylab = "Colony Area",
     main = paste("Best model:", best_name))
lines(pgrid, preds, col = "red", lwd = 2)
# Add other model predictions for comparison
preds_quad <- predict(m_quad, newdata = data.frame(prop287 = pgrid))
preds_cubic <- predict(m_cubic, newdata = data.frame(prop287 = pgrid))
preds_ns <- predict(m_ns, newdata = data.frame(prop287 = pgrid))
lines(pgrid, preds_quad, col = "blue", lwd = 1, lty = 2)
lines(pgrid, preds_cubic, col = "green", lwd = 1, lty = 3)
lines(pgrid, preds_ns, col = "orange", lwd = 1, lty = 4)
legend("topleft",
       legend = c(best_name, "Quadratic", "Cubic", "Natural Spline"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "green", "orange"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 3, 4), lwd = c(2, 1, 1, 1))
dev.off()

cat("\nDone.\n")
